tools.name: lbb_rdf
tools.description: Store and extend complete RDF/OWL documents through MCP. import accepts Turtle/N-Triples/N-Quads/TriG without conversion; update executes INSERT DATA for additive edits. Replacing/removing axioms is unsupported; use a new versioned LBB graph for a revised document. Named RDF graphs are unsupported; Turtle/N-Triples use the default graph, and dataset formats must contain only default-graph quads. These write graph facts, distinct from lbb_configure's native schema metadata. A first RDF write selects RDF-native storage, which refuses later property-graph commits; choose the write workflow before bootstrap. Retries deduplicate by content unless idempotency_key is supplied. A completed write schedules publication; inspect action=publication and verify using lbb_query entailment=owl. An update with DELETE, CLEAR, DROP, MOVE or COPY asks the person to approve it first; the question quotes the operations that remove. The server asks the person to approve it through the client (MCP form elicitation) and sends nothing when they decline (approval_declined). A client that cannot show the question gets approval_required and nothing is sent, unless the MCP server's environment sets LBB_MCP_DESTRUCTIVE=allow.

tools.name: lbb_files
tools.description: Files of the graph, read only. A file is a document the graph holds (its bytes and a Document entity); the documents.parse workflow (lbb_workflows) reads the text layer of each PDF into pages with every line and its box. list shows 50 files a call, newest upload first, with their sha256, name, size, Document IRI and parse (status parsed, unsupported or failed, page_count); when more follow, next names the after of the next call (with the same filters). parse_status keeps the files of one parse status; waiting is a file not parsed yet. name keeps the files whose name holds a text, in any case. A filtered list reads the Documents of the published generation and names its commit (as_of_commit_seq). A file uploaded, renamed or parsed a moment ago can be missing from it until publication. pages reads parsed pages of one file (sha256, or name for an exact file name): from is the first 0-based page index (the page of a region and of a DocEntry or DocMention), to the page after the last one (default from+1). Each line comes as `<line id> [x0,y0,x1,y1] <text>`: the id is p<page number>-l<line number>, both from 1, and the box is normalized to the page (0 to 1, origin top left). contains keeps the lines that hold a text; max_lines caps the lines (default 200). When lines were left out, next names the from and line_offset of the next call. A file not parsed yet answers file_not_parsed.

parse_status.description: list: only the files of this parse status; waiting is a file not parsed yet.

tools.name: lbb_reviews
tools.description: Review items, read only: questions for a person (human in the loop) that workflows, integrations, agents and people file. Kinds and their decisions: change (accept an ontology change, identities or facts: accept, reject, cant_tell), value (confirm one value of a property, question.property and question.value: accept, correct with the right value, reject, cant_tell; accept and correct commit the value), choice (pick one of question.options: choose with option, cant_tell), grade (grade question.output on the scale question.options: choose with option, cant_tell), answer (answer question.prompt in words: accept with the text in note, cant_tell). Status is open, answered or withdrawn. Scope is live (default) or test: a test item writes nothing. list returns one page as the server sends it ({object, data, has_more, next_cursor}), the latest update first: pass next_cursor as cursor, with the same filters, for the next page. get reads one item (rev_…) with its question, evidence, answer and effects. patterns groups the live items that ask one decision, the largest first. Evals files the questions of model checks (origin_id evals:checks), calibration sessions (evals:calibration) and golden queries (evals:golden) as grade and choice items; eval_id keeps the items of one record, and their answer is the record's label. File, answer, comment on or withdraw items with lbb_reviews_manage.

tools.name: lbb_reviews_manage
tools.description: File, answer, comment on or withdraw review items. Show the item to the user and answer only what the user decided. Kinds and their decisions: change (accept an ontology change, identities or facts: accept, reject, cant_tell), value (confirm one value of a property, question.property and question.value: accept, correct with the right value, reject, cant_tell; accept and correct commit the value), choice (pick one of question.options: choose with option, cant_tell), grade (grade question.output on the scale question.options: choose with option, cant_tell), answer (answer question.prompt in words: accept with the text in note, cant_tell). Status is open, answered or withdrawn. Scope is live (default) or test: a test item writes nothing. An answer that accepts or corrects a value item, or accepts a change item, commits facts or applies an ontology change (which can remove types and relations): the server reads the items and asks the person to approve first, with the count and the effect. Any other answer, such as the grade or choice of an item Evals filed, asks nothing. The server asks the person to approve it through the client (MCP form elicitation) and sends nothing when they decline (approval_declined). A client that cannot show the question gets approval_required and nothing is sent, unless the MCP server's environment sets LBB_MCP_DESTRUCTIVE=allow. create files an item of kind value, choice, grade or answer (kind, title, question, and optionally subject, evidence, rationale, key, scope, facts, origin); the same key again updates it, and an answered item comes back unchanged. File an ontology change with lbb_configure action=suggest_ontology_change. answer records the person's answer (decision, with value for correct, option for choose, note). An item has one answer: the same answer again returns the item, another one answers 409 review_answered. revision is the revision the person saw; a later one answers 409 review_stale. answer_batch gives one answer to up to 500 ids. comment adds text to an item's discussion. withdraw takes back an item you filed, with a reason. Each write sends an idempotency key, and a retry after a network failure or a 5xx sends the same key, so the write happens once.

tools.name: lbb_inspect
tools.description: Read graph context and exact graph facts. Actions: guide, graphs, publication, ontology, ontology_conformance, schema, ontology_search, metadata, entity, ontology_suggestions. graphs works before bootstrap; ontology_suggestions lists the ontology change suggestions that wait for review (or were decided); fact_count is how many graph facts (triplets and entity property rows) accepting one commits, and identity_count how many identities it links. publication reports whether writes are queryable. ontology and schema return complete entries with page_size, section and cursor; follow next until absent. schema reads active native ontology/SHACL metadata without running validation. Query asserted RDF/OWL axioms separately with lbb_query. ontology_conformance serves the durable report referenced by the pinned published root. entity with iri, or version=records/1 and entity_id or entity_type+key, returns a complete exact-term record, separate assertions and snapshot from RDF. as_of_commit_seq pins retained history; schema-bound historical selection is currently unsupported. Oversized records fail rather than truncate. Omitting the new selectors preserves the native attributes/relationships view. Use lbb_query with SPARQL property paths for precise path selection.

action.description: Selects the variant (one of: guide, ontology, ontology_conformance, schema, graphs, publication, ontology_search, metadata, ontology_suggestions, entity).

detail.description: Response detail level. Defaults to compact.

graph.description: Graph to target; defaults to the connection's graph

status.description: Only suggestions in this state; default all

key.description: Stable key with entity_type, resolved from the activated schema at the read snapshot.

as_of_commit_seq.description: Snapshot pin: reproduce the node's attributes and relationships as of this commit_seq.

tools.name: lbb_query
tools.description: Analytical and expert reads. Modes: question (a question in plain words), structured (SPARQL-subset JSON body), sparql (SPARQL text), search (instances by meaning over every searchable class; filter narrows by class and relationship; every hit checked against the graph), analyze, and four tools for writing your own queries: names, describe, commit_at, compare. names: before a query that names an entity (a person, a company), find its IRI with text=<the question or the names>; use the first candidate, not a CONTAINS match on the name. describe: before a query on classes or properties you have not seen, read them with question=<the question> (or classes/properties as IRIs): how many sampled instances hold each property (a filter on a rare one returns few rows), the values of small classes such as stages, examples and schema statements. commit_at: for a question about a date, find the commit of date=YYYY-MM-DD (or moment=RFC 3339), then run mode=sparql as_of_commit_seq=<it>. compare: for what changed between two points, run one SELECT at before and after (default the latest) with key=[the entity variable]; added, removed and changed come with totals and pages (next). Use mode=question when you have a question in plain words and no SPARQL query: the server picks the kind of question (route), runs queries in a bounded loop, reads their rows, and answers in plain words (about 8 s). The result holds the answer with citations and a chart hint (kind, x, y: columns of the rows), the steps, the route, and the query and rows the answer stands on. Continue or correct that query with mode=sparql. Each question uses model tokens and counts toward a daily limit of the stack. SPARQL is the query language; search finds what the words describe. SPARQL text can also search by meaning inside the query with ?x <https://littlebigbrain.com/search#similarTo> "words", so the other patterns filter and join the hits in one query; the result's search field reports the plan. To plan a search: lbb_embeddings action=list, then SPARQL for a class's relationships on a sample, then mode=search with explain=true to check the resolved filter before the real search (lbb_inspect action=guide has the queries). Use the exact IRIs returned by names, describe or RDF. Native records use content-addressed entity IRIs, <https://littlebigbrain.com/r/NAME> relations and <https://littlebigbrain.com/class/NAME> types (lowercased); imported RDF may use any vocabulary. Never build an entity IRI from a display name. Structured and text queries pin one published watermark for the request.

mode.description: Selects the variant (one of: structured, sparql, question, search, analyze, names, describe, commit_at, compare).

consistency.description: Read consistency. strong requires publication through head; a pending response is retryable.

min_indexed_seq.description: Read-after-write publication floor. Preserved across cursor pages.

body.description: Structured SPARQL-subset request body. Shape: { patterns: [{ subject, predicate, object }], filters?, group_by?, group_keys?, aggregates?, having?, order_by?, select?, limit?, distinct? }. Each pattern term is { var: "x" } or a fixed { entity: { entity_type, name } }; `predicate` is a relation name and is case-insensitive here (FOR_CLIENT and for_client both resolve — unlike SPARQL text, which needs the lowercased IRI local name). FILTER — `filters` is a list of conditions, each of exact shape { "compare": { "op": <op>, "left": <term>, "right": <term> } } (or { "and": [<filter>…] }, { "or": [<filter>…] }, { "not": <filter> }). `op` is one of eq | ne | lt | le | gt | ge (NOT the symbols =,<,>). Each <term> is exactly one of { "var": "x" }, { "property": { "var": "x", "field": "amount" } } (a typed scalar attribute), or { "value": <typed> } — and <typed> is exactly one wrapper: { "str": "…" }, { "i64": 5 }, { "f64": 0.9 }, { "bool": true }, { "date_time": "2026-01-01" } (RFC3339), or { "entity": { "entity_type": "T", "name": "N" } }. Complete runnable example — deals whose amount ≥ 1000000: { "patterns": [{ "subject": { "var": "d" }, "predicate": "for_client", "object": { "var": "c" } }], "filters": [{ "compare": { "op": "ge", "left": { "property": { "var": "d", "field": "amount" } }, "right": { "value": { "f64": 1000000 } } } }] }. Comparisons use the field's real declared type (numbers as numbers, datetimes as instants), so they run server-side. GROUP BY supports both entity-identity keys (group_by: ["s"]) and typed scalar keys via group_keys: a property value ({ property: { var, field, as } }) or a calendar bucket of a datetime property ({ date_bucket: { var, field, granularity: year|month|week|day|hour, as } }). Scalar keys come back per group under value_keys[as] — so a per-area breakdown or a commits-per-month time series is one server-side query, no client-side bucketing. Worked example -- commits per area per month in one query: { "patterns": [{ "subject": { "var": "c" }, "predicate": "committed_to", "object": { "var": "repo" } }], "group_keys": [{ "date_bucket": { "var": "c", "field": "committed_at", "granularity": "month", "as": "m" } }, { "property": { "var": "c", "field": "area", "as": "area" } }], "aggregates": [{ "func": "count", "as": "n" }], "order_by": [{ "var": "m" }] } -- area and committed_at are typed entity attributes (set via entity_properties; readable flat under attributes, never a nested metadata blob), and each group returns value_keys.m + value_keys.area + aggregates.n. `having: [...]` takes the same filter shape over the aggregated groups (e.g. { "compare": { "op": "gt", "left": { "var": "n" }, "right": { "value": { "i64": 10 } } } }). A `combinators` key (UNION/OPTIONAL/MINUS/EXISTS) is rejected here; express those with SPARQL text under mode=sparql. Cheap aggregate count: pair an equality having (e.g. { "compare": { "op": "eq", "left": { "var": "n" }, "right": { "value": { "i64": 4 } } } }) with row_limit: 1 -- the response row_page.total reports how many groups match without materializing them all, so you read the count off row_page.total instead of paging every matching row. For snapshot pinning use the top-level `as_of_commit_seq` argument or the same body field. Valid-time `as_of` and `as_of_valid_time` selectors are unsupported and rejected before HTTP.

as_of.description: Unsupported in structured and SPARQL text modes; use as_of_commit_seq for a retained commit snapshot.

as_of_commit_seq.description: Snapshot pin: evaluate the body as of this commit_seq, hiding later commits. Errors if past head. Top-level alias for the body's `as_of_commit_seq` (either works for this one).

row_limit.description: Maximum query rows to return in this page. Defaults by detail: compact=20, standard=100, full=1000.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous lbb_query row page; reruns the original query at the next offset.

detail.description: Response detail level. Defaults to compact.

graph.description: Graph to target; defaults to the connection's graph

entailment.description: Reasoning over the pinned RDF generation. Defaults to none. owl includes RDFS, inverse relationships and the supported OWL profile.

query.description: SPARQL 1.1 query text (SELECT or ASK). Valid-time as_of is unsupported; use as_of_commit_seq for a retained commit snapshot. Imported RDF retains its exact, case-sensitive IRIs. Use returned IRIs unchanged; lbb_inspect action=entity iri=<full IRI> reads any subject with records/1. The following convention applies only to native records: relations are <https://littlebigbrain.com/r/NAME> (NAME lowercased, e.g. writes_to; reverse a relation with the ^ path operator, no stored inverse triple). Types are <https://littlebigbrain.com/class/NAME> (lowercased), matched as `?x a <…/class/NAME>` with explicit entailment=subclass, rdfs, or owl for inference (default none). Property fields are <https://littlebigbrain.com/p/NAME> (lowercased). The local name is ALWAYS lowercase — an uppercase one (e.g. <…/r/FOR_CLIENT>) is a different, non-existent IRI that silently matches nothing; this tool auto-lowercases the local name of /r/, /class/, and /p/ IRIs for you and adds a `notes` entry when it does, so a stray uppercase still resolves. (Structured mode's `predicate` is case-insensitive on its own.) Entities are content-addressed <https://littlebigbrain.com/e/HASH> — never build an entity IRI from a name; anchor a named entity by its label instead: `?e <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label> "Acme"`. Discover the exact relation and type names with lbb_inspect action=ontology. SELECT and ASK only (CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE are rejected). Example: SELECT ?service ?db WHERE { ?service <https://littlebigbrain.com/r/writes_to> ?db } LIMIT 10. Search by meaning inside the query (the graph needs an embedding; see lbb_embeddings action=list): PREFIX search: <https://littlebigbrain.com/search#> SELECT ?x ?score WHERE { ?x search:similarTo "card payments" ; search:score ?score . ?x <https://littlebigbrain.com/r/calls> ?y } ORDER BY DESC(?score) LIMIT 5. The other patterns filter and join the hits. One search:similarTo per query, with a variable subject, in the main group (not inside OPTIONAL, UNION, MINUS or a subquery). The object is text, an entity IRI (records like that one) or a vector literal. search:top N sets the hits (1 to 1000; default the query LIMIT, then 10) and search:embedding "name" searches one embedding. FILTER(?score > 0.8) keeps close hits. The result's search field reports the plan (nearest, filter_first or search_first), the hits and complete. For a question in words, add search:rerank true ; search:relevance ?r and ORDER BY DESC(?r): the rerank model (Jev) reads the best hits with the text, keeps the top that answer it and binds its answer (0 to 1); search.rerank reports the status. Only a text query reranks. compare: the SELECT to run at both points; leave out LIMIT.

request.description: The user's own words behind this query (managed evals). When present the server records an eval trace and the result carries its trace_id; label the rows valid or not with lbb_evals action=label. Omit on continuation pages.

question.description: question: the question in plain words (required), 1 to 4,000 characters. The server's model runs queries on this graph, reads their rows, and answers. describe: the question whose classes and properties to describe.

context.description: question: notes for the model, at most 8,000 characters: what the data means, units, names to prefer.

route.description: question: the kind of question, when you know it. Omit it and the router model picks it.

limit.description: question: rows each query of the server's loop returns, 1 to 1,000. Defaults by detail: compact=20, standard=100, full=1000. names: candidates per name, 1 to 10 (default 5). compare: entries of each list per page, 1 to 1,000 (defaults by detail: 20, 100, 500).

anchor.description: question: entity IRIs the question is about, at most 10 (for example the record the user has open). The server reads each one, and its queries use these IRIs directly instead of matching their names.

timeline.description: question: dated points that stand for the graph's commits, at most 200. A question about a date reads the commit of the latest point on or before it. Use it when the commits stand for other dates than the days they were written (a demo's milestones, an import of old records); without it the server reads the last commit written by the end of that day.

as_of_commit_seq.description: The commit that holds the graph as it was on that date.

label.description: A name for the point, such as a milestone.

embedding.description: One embedding by name (see lbb_embeddings action=list). Omit it to search every searchable class of the graph; each hit names its class.

text.description: search: the query text (required); embedded with the graph's model. names: the question, or the names, to find (required).

probe.description: Clusters to read (default 4·√clusters, at least 8). More reads cost latency and find more.

include.description: text: return the embedded text of each hit.

filter.description: Conditions every hit must meet: {"class": …} or {"via": …, "to": …}. The response's filter shows how each condition resolved; an unknown relationship or name answers with the options.

class.description: A class condition: one class IRI or a list (any of); subclasses too. One class condition per search.

via.description: A relationship condition: the relationship, a local name (calls), prefix:name, or <iri>.

to.description: With via: the entity, an IRI or a name (its label; a spelling slip resolves when one entity is clearly closest), or a list (any of).

direction.description: With via: out (default), the hit links to the entity; in, the entity links to the hit.

explain.description: Plan without running: the scope, the resolved filter, and the allowed count. No model call.

rerank.description: true: the managed rerank model (Jev) orders the best hits by how well each answers the text, and each hit gets its relevance (0 to 1); adds about 0.3 s. false: the similarity order. Omit it to follow the graph's search setting.

classes.description: describe: class IRIs to describe, at most 20.

properties.description: describe: property IRIs to describe, at most 50.

date.description: commit_at: YYYY-MM-DD; the last commit written by the end of that day (UTC).

moment.description: commit_at: RFC 3339, e.g. 2026-06-18T12:00:00Z; the last commit written at or before it.

before.description: compare: the earlier point (required): {"as_of_commit_seq": n}, {"date": "YYYY-MM-DD"} or {"moment": "RFC 3339"}.

after.description: compare: the later point; defaults to the latest commit.

key.description: compare: the variables that identify a row's entity, e.g. ["contact"]. With a key the rows are paired: added and removed hold the entities at one point only, changed the entities whose values differ. Without one whole rows are compared.

max_rows.description: compare: rows to read per point, 1 to 50,000 (default 20,000). Past it the result says truncated.

compare_cursor.description: compare: the cursor of the page before, from next; pass it with the same arguments.

tools.name: lbb_models
tools.description: Read model-training inputs or compare retrieval configurations over one pinned published snapshot, or read what the managed models did. shadow_eval takes the API ShadowEvalRequest body; dataset actions return bounded training examples at an optional signal split. activity reads one month of the stack's model use (all graphs): calls, items, estimated tokens and cost per feature (index, search, fit, judge, training, rerank, rewrite, trial, workflows) and model, by day and by graph, the workflows' calls per workflow and job (by_workflow), the months with activity, and the model each feature uses now.

month.description: activity: the month, yyyy-mm (UTC). Defaults to the current month.

detail.description: Response detail level. Defaults to compact.

graph.description: Graph to target; defaults to the connection's graph

tools.name: lbb_embeddings
tools.description: Search setup, read only: embeddings declared on classes (an embedding on a class covers its subclasses; one model per graph). list shows each embedding's status (serving and building version, backfill progress, lag) and the graph's model; get shows one; preview shows every candidate fact of a class with its coverage and examples, and the exact text of sample instances, and stores nothing. Declare, refresh, or change the model with lbb_embeddings_manage; search with lbb_query mode=search. list is the first step of planning a search (lbb_inspect action=guide has the recipe).

name.description: get: the embedding name.

from.description: preview/declare: the fields, e.g. ["label", "description", "calls/label"]. Omit for the automatic choice; on an existing embedding, omit to keep its fields.

tools.name: lbb_workflows
tools.description: Starter workflows and triggered workflows, read only. A starter workflow is a template; a triggered workflow is a workflow created from one on the graph. It watches a class: when a published commit adds or changes instances of the class (or changes the watched fields), the workflow reads them and does its work. search.embed keeps an embedding of the class (the same as lbb_embeddings); ontology.fit reads text fields and files ontology suggestions (the same as lbb_fit_sources); workflow (a developer workflow) sends the new and changed instances to a workflow of the developer's worker as trigger messages, and that code writes the facts the workflow owns. documents.parse reads uploaded PDF files into pages with line boxes, documents.link connects mentions of the same thing across the documents (it writes DocEntry and DocMention instances and links each mention to the entry that defines or describes it), documents.map proposes each link as a FactProposal in the graph's own ontology (fact_subject, fact_predicate, fact_object, fact_confidence, fact_evidence) for a review workflow, and values.extract fills chosen properties from text, each value with a quote; read the files and their pages with lbb_files. starters lists the starter workflows this server offers with their group, settings and whether each can run here. list shows every triggered workflow of the graph with its state (backfilling, ready, paused, failed, unavailable), lag, counters, this month's spend and last error; get shows one (starter and name) with its own status in details (for workflow: the messages sent, the instances waiting, the message in flight and whether it is paused). preview shows what creating one would do (the resolved watch, the instance count and the workflow's own preview; for workflow, the first messages it would send), calls no model and stores nothing. workflows lists the same workflows as workflows with triggers (/v1/workflows/named): each one's target workflow type (LBB's own are lbb.* types), its shards (engine identities starter.<name> and starter.<name>.<k>), its routing field, its window, its one watch trigger, its status and each shard's inbox, one page in data (has_more and next_cursor page them with cursor and limit); name for one. queue (name) shows what a workflow's watch has not sent yet: each waiting instance with its shard and its origin (a backfill, a commit range with the watched fields and the requests that changed it, a run now, a schema change), the pass in progress, and per shard its message in flight and its first unfinished turns with their origins; the items are in data, and has_more and next_cursor page them with cursor and limit. run_results (name) shows what the workflow's runs did with each input, newest run first: the input's IRI and label, its outcome (written, review, no_value, failed, duplicate) and its values (the value, the quote that states it, its support, the conversion, and the review item it went to); run keeps one run (with run_counts, every input by outcome), outcome keeps some outcomes, iri keeps one input; data, has_more and next_cursor page them. A run records its results when it ends; they are kept 30 days. revisions (name) shows the history of a workflow's settings, newest change first: each item is a revision (settings, the request that makes it, and an id wrev_… that is the hash of the settings) with who changed it, when, how (create, change, activate, existing) and bound (the one in use); a row whose revision was deleted has available false and no settings; has_more and next_cursor page it with cursor and limit (1 to 100, default 20). revision (name, revision) reads one revision; compare two by their settings to say what changed. Each run summary names the revision it ran on. Message workflows of the workflow engine are not listed here. tests lists the graph's workflow tests, newest first, without texts and results (name: one workflow's tests), one page with next_cursor; tests_get reads one test (id) with its inputs' texts and, per input, each value read with its quote, its support and what the live workflow does with it (writes it, gives it to review, or drops it). A test goes queued, running, then done, failed or cancelled. Create, refresh, pause or resume with lbb_workflows_manage, which also starts, answers and cancels tests and goes back to an earlier revision with its action activate; delete with lbb_workflows_delete.

tools.name: lbb_workflows_manage
tools.description: Create a workflow from a starter workflow, or refresh, pause or resume a triggered workflow. Run lbb_workflows action=preview first and show the user the watch and the instance count. use creates a workflow from a starter workflow of action=starters, under a name (default: the class's local name), with its watch (class, fields) and params; the workflow then reads every instance of the class and follows each published commit. A developer workflow (starter=workflow) also takes workflow (workflow_type and version of the developer's worker), owns and batch; it needs a server with the workflow engine. use again with the same starter and name changes only what you name, and the same request again changes nothing. A workflow that calls models (ontology.fit, documents.link, documents.map, values.extract) spends model budget as it reads. refresh asks the workflow to run now and returns at once with queued; poll lbb_workflows action=get for progress. pause stops a workflow (a developer workflow, documents.parse, documents.link, documents.map or values.extract) from reading and sending, and stops the claims of a developer workflow's shards; resume lets it catch up. Without starter, pause and resume name a workflow with triggers. search.embed and ontology.fit cannot be paused. define creates or changes a workflow with triggers of the developer's worker (/v1/workflows/named): name, workflow, one trigger (class and fields for a watch, media_types for a content trigger on uploads, schedule for one run per slot of a timer, or stream for the events a client sends, in batches), owns, batch, and shards (engine identities, 1 to 16), route_by (a field that keeps work in order) and window (messages queued per shard, default 4), and optionally budget_usd_per_month (the workflow's own monthly model budget), on_exhausted (block or skip) and fan_in (the id of a fan-in identity the shards send to); it needs a server with the workflow engine, and a change of shards waits for empty inboxes. run (name) runs a workflow with triggers now: its watch sends every instance again, a content trigger reads its log again, a schedule sends one run outside its slots, a stream sends its partial batches. activate (name, revision) makes an earlier revision of a workflow's settings (from lbb_workflows action=revisions) the one in use: it goes through the same checks as a change, and answers the workflow with its active_revision. Show the user what changes first (compare the settings of the two revisions), and pass expected_revision, the revision you read as bound, so a change by someone else since fails with workflow_revision_conflict. A revision whose settings the graph now reads differently fails with workflow_revision_stale; then change the workflow instead. Activating changes what the workflow does from then on and deletes no data, so it is not a destructive write; a change of the watch, the parameters or the gate makes the workflow read its class again, and work that waits or runs keeps the revision it started with. tests_create tests a values.extract workflow on chosen inputs before it writes: name (a workflow of the graph; starter defaults to values.extract) or install (a workflow not created yet, as use takes it: starter, name, watch, params, gate), and iris (at most 20) or sample (1 to 20, default 6), and models to try other models before choosing one. A test reads each input as the workflow would and calls its models (the calls count in the monthly workflow budget); it writes nothing to the graph. Poll lbb_workflows action=tests_get. tests_answer records the person's answer to one value of a read input (id, iri, property, answer: accept, reject, correct with value, or cant_tell; null removes it); it writes nothing to the graph. Answer only what the user decided. tests_cancel stops a queued or running test (id). Save a test's answers as a dataset with lbb_evals action=datasets_create.

tools.name: lbb_model_choice
tools.description: Model choice, read only: which model each use of a model on the graph runs, and trials that test other models against the graph's ground truth (the checked calls: a person's review, else the judge's verdict). options shows per use the model it runs now (current), LBB's model (default), a switch (switched), its checked calls, and the models a trial can test with their efforts, prices and whether the server holds their key; available=false with a reason when trials cannot run. trials lists the trials, newest first, each with its report: calls compared, both models' right share, mean score (0 to 1), cost per call and median time, the difference with its 95% interval (delta, ci_low, ci_high), outcome (too_few, better, same, worse) and qualifies (meets the bar: at least 20 calls, at most 5 points worse at the low end, no more failures, cheaper or better). trial reads one trial with its compared calls; trial_call reads one call with both answers and the ground truth. switches lists the switched uses. choices lists the model choices of the workflow uses (extract, decide, embed): without workflow the environment's row of each use and each workflow's own choice; with workflow the row in force for each of its uses (its own, else the environment's, else the default). A row has scope (environment or workflow), model, source (person or default), since, by, the model before, the use's default and options (the models it can run, with efforts, list prices and whether the server holds their key). One page in data: has_more and next_cursor page it with cursor and limit. Start, stop, switch or revert, and set or remove a choice, with lbb_model_choice_manage.

tools.name: lbb_model_choice_manage
tools.description: Model choice, writes. start tests a candidate model on the uses in jobs (without jobs, every use it can do that has checked calls): the server answers those checked calls again with the candidate and scores it and the model in use against the same ground truth. It changes no model and spends at most the trial budget ($3.00 by default) of model and judge cost; an open trial of the same use and candidate comes back as it is. Pick candidates from lbb_model_choice action=options (provider anthropic with an effort, or typesafe jev-latest). A trial runs by itself: poll lbb_model_choice action=trial until its status is no longer running. stop ends a trial; it keeps what it compared. switch makes the trial's use run its candidate on this graph from the next call on; only a trial that qualifies and compared with the model in use switches (ask to a Claude model, route to a Jev model). Show the user the trial's report (score, difference and interval, cost per call, time) and switch only what the user confirmed. revert puts the use back on LBB's model. put_choice chooses the model of a workflow use (use extract or decide, provider, model, effort) for the environment, or for one workflow with workflow: the next calls run it. Pick the model from the row's options in lbb_model_choice action=choices, show the user the price per million tokens of the model in use and of the new one, and set only what the user confirmed. delete_choice removes a choice: the use runs the environment's choice, else its default; it answers {id, object, deleted: true}. Both change only the model of future calls and remove no data, so neither asks for approval.

tools.name: lbb_evals
tools.description: Managed evals: ground truth for the questions an app asks and the searches it runs. A query run with `request` (lbb_query, also mode=question) records a trace: the question, the query that answered it, the type of that query (`query_type`: sparql, hybrid = search by meaning with conditions, search = search by meaning alone) and one item per result (hit or row); trace reads it back with the item ids. label has two forms. On a question's trace, valid alone judges the whole answer: valid=true makes the trace's query the golden query of the question; valid=false with sparql gives the right query, which becomes the golden query; valid=false alone marks the answer wrong; route with valid=true (or valid=false with sparql) names the route the question expects, and valid=true alone takes the trace's route. item + valid (or items) judges one result, a citation of the answer: the ground truth of the hits of a search by meaning, and a result marked wrong must not come back for any type. golden freezes a stored query or a search (every result it returns now is relevant). run checks every golden at the current commit: a question is asked again through the query rewriter, then the type of the query it wrote is compared with the expected type, its rows with the rows of the golden query at the same commit (`query_check`), and its results with the judged results, and the router's pick with the golden's route (route_check, which does not change the verdict); a search is done again; new results open a review trace. run_answers checks your own app's answers instead: ask each question golden's request with your own loop, then send answers=[{golden, sparql, route}] (route = the route of lbb_query mode=question with route mode, sparql absent for an unanswerable question, error for a failure); the server runs each query and checks it the same way, and the runs form the app's own series (runner; results with runner reads them). judge lets the platform's judge model (the hosted frontier model) label unlabeled results. summary, traces, goldens, results, and settings read state. Model checks: a judge model checks a sample of the model calls LBB makes for the graph (rerank, route, ask = the answer of a question, rewrite, fit, propose, label). checks_summary reads a month per job and model (checks, score, right, partly, wrong, reviews) and the judge's agreement with people; checks lists the month's checks, newest first, with the judge's verdict, score and reason and the ground truth (`truth`). review_check records a person's review of one check (call_id): agree=true keeps the judge's verdict; agree=false with verdict (and an optional score, reference and note) corrects it. The review becomes the call's ground truth, so show the check to the user and review only what the user confirmed. Datasets: named sets of examples with the outputs a correct run gives, which workflow tests and template evals share. The kind values holds per item an input text (name, text, iri), the property values a correct run writes (values) and those it must leave out (leave_out). datasets lists the graph's datasets, newest first, without their items (one page with next_cursor); datasets_get reads one (id) with its items; datasets_export returns it as a template's samples, records (records.json) and expected (expected.json). datasets_create makes one with name and items (at most 500), install (the settings it is graded with: each property's value type, units, context) and about, or from a workflow test's answers with source={kind: test, id}. datasets_items adds items to a dataset (id); an item with the name of one it holds replaces it. Delete a dataset with lbb_evals_delete, which asks the person first. A dataset ends with its graph.

tools.name: lbb_commit
tools.description: Write graph facts, retract them, or label ranked results. mode=facts writes triplets/embeddings/properties; mode=retract removes a wrongly-added fact (by edge or by entity) without a full reset; mode=search_feedback stores query/result relevance labels (Feedback grades: 3=ideal/good, 1=partial, 0=bad; include query, search_id when available, target, rank, score). Explicit idempotency_key wins; when omitted, MCP derives a stable content hash so content-identical retries dedupe. Facts mode defaults edge_idempotency to append; pass skip_unchanged for re-runnable backfills. A retract asks the person to approve the links and records it removes first. The server asks the person to approve it through the client (MCP form elicitation) and sends nothing when they decline (approval_declined). A client that cannot show the question gets approval_required and nothing is sent, unless the MCP server's environment sets LBB_MCP_DESTRUCTIVE=allow.

tools.name: lbb_configure
tools.description: Manage native schema metadata. Actions: define_ontology (friendly spec with super_types), evolve_ontology (ordered edits including add_super_types), list_starters (the base ontologies crm, documents and work, each with its status on the graph: absent, partial or applied, what applying adds, and conflicts), apply_starter (add what the graph lacks of a starter in one ontology version; a relation the graph has is widened; refused with starter_conflict when the graph holds a term differently; dry_run previews), publish_schema (SHACL activation), suggest_ontology_change (file a change for a person to review instead of applying it; prefer it when the graph's owner reviews ontology changes, and list the result with lbb_inspect action=ontology_suggestions; facts files graph facts for review, which accepting commits after the change, and change may be empty when facts is set), get_rewrite_profile and set_rewrite_profile (the graph's notes and up to 20 worked question-to-SPARQL examples that lbb_query mode=question reads for every question; pass the version you read as expected_version). define, evolve, publish and set_rewrite_profile support dry_run previews. Definition/import here extracts native metadata; it does NOT store the complete RDF/OWL document as queryable graph facts. Use lbb_rdf import for full OWL and lbb_rdf update for additive INSERT DATA revisions; RDF deletions are unsupported. Publish_schema accepts unchanged ontology plus shapes; use define/evolve for native ontology changes. Publication enqueues durable conformance; a preview does not validate the whole graph. An evolve_ontology that removes (remove_entity_type, remove_relation, or narrow_relation with remove_domain or remove_range) and a publish_schema with desired_mode=reject ask the person to approve first; a dry_run does not ask. The server asks the person to approve it through the client (MCP form elicitation) and sends nothing when they decline (approval_declined). A client that cannot show the question gets approval_required and nothing is sent, unless the MCP server's environment sets LBB_MCP_DESTRUCTIVE=allow.
